claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct enforced entirely within Pulumi and is never sent to the cloud provider.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute, a cloud-provider deletion-protection attribute enforced by the cloud provider independently of Pulumi.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute, a cloud-provider deletion-protection attribute enforced by the cloud provider independently of Pulumi.

A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (protect not set) and still refuse to be deleted because of provider-side deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi while the provider-side deletion protection is off.

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider-side deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` resource option.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection independent of Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection independent of Pulumi's `protect` option.
Pulumi's `protect` option and a resource's own provider/cloud-API deletion-protection attributes are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The Pulumi docs page on destroy-failures troubleshooting (/docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/) has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell `protect` and resource-level deletion protection apart and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Three distinct layers can hold deletion protection that causes a `pulumi destroy` failure: Pulumi's protect option, a provider-enforced flag, and a cloud-API-enforced protection.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove `protect`.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call when a resource has a deletion-protection attribute, e.g. `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster`; the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` property.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and Azure Resource Manager management locks are enforced by the cloud API itself, which rejects the delete call independent of Pulumi.
Azure Resource Manager returns an error code such as `ScopeLocked` when deleting a resource under a management lock.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says, so setting the attribute to false in the program alone is not enough.

Remediation for provider-enforced and cloud-enforced deletion protection: set the attribute to false in the program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches the live resource and state, then run `pulumi destroy`.
If deletion protection was already disabled outside Pulumi, `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has `deletionProtection` enforced by the provider, and a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` `deletionProtection` is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is true.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` `deletionProtection` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to false.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` `forceDestroy` defaults to false, and a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` `disableApiTermination` is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` `deletionProtectionEnabled` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to false.

`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist; a `CanNotDelete` lock enforced by Azure Resource Manager must be removed before the resource can be deleted.

Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered, and purge protection prevents purging until its retention period elapses.
